source_request_policy.global_opt_in: EXTERNAL_REQUESTS_ENABLED defaults to false and gates all external polling, chart retrieval, Jev calls, and operator retry.
source_request_policy.source_allowlist: EXTERNAL_SOURCE_COLLECTORS defaults to empty. When global opt-in is true, only listed real collectors can poll; yahoo_quote and yahoo_chart are separate allowlist entries.
source_request_policy.jev_forwarding: TYPESAFE_ALLOWED_COLLECTORS is intersected with EXTERNAL_SOURCE_COLLECTORS. Jev may receive a source item only when its collector is explicitly admitted by both lists, a non-empty key is configured, and both finite daily budgets are positive. The effective set gates startup and scheduled drains, new ingestion, and operator retry.
source_request_policy.verification: The fresh-process offline verifier proves the saved-data default makes zero external fetch attempts. It launches one isolated process per collector with only that collector allowlisted, checks the expected request URL shape and exact health/delivery gates, and intercepts every external global fetch before network access. A separate mismatch case supplies an API key, positive finite budgets, and a Jev allowlist that does not intersect the active source allowlist; Jev health must remain disabled.

current_followup.result: The SEC's current Webmaster FAQ says EDGAR public filing content is free to access and reuse, and its Website Dissemination policy says sec.gov information may be copied or further distributed without SEC permission. This supports a narrow evaluation path using public EDGAR filing content. It is not blanket rights clearance for non-EDGAR publisher text, an SEC endorsement, or authorization to use a TypeSafe account.
sec_conditions: For the initial path, use public EDGAR filing content only; omit SEC marks/artwork and avoid any clearly third-party material embedded in a filing.
Configure a descriptive SEC User-Agent that identifies the operator and includes contact information; the SEC says automated tools must be classified.
Stay at or below the SEC limit of 10 requests per second aggregated across machines; the app's 125ms per-process start spacing is below this limit, but multiple processes are not coordinated.

Use a TypeSafe account authorized by its owner and confirm the current agreement, account limits, auto-refill, retention, telemetry, rejected-request billing, and that the intended product use fits the similar/competing-product restriction before dispatch.
current_followup.type_safe_billing: The MCA currently posted as last updated 2026-09-23 says credits are consumed by each submitted Input, and account settings control consumption/refills. The reviewed API documentation describes 429 and 529 retry behavior but does not say those submissions are free. Treat them as potentially billable until the authorized account owner verifies the account's actual billing behavior.
current_followup.type_safe_data_use: The current MCA grants TypeSafe processing of Input to provide the service and broad, perpetual processing of Customer Data to derive Telemetry; Telemetry includes hashes, summary statistics, classifications, metrics, and learnings, and may be used without restriction to improve TypeSafe products. The privacy policy says Inputs are not used to train or fine-tune models, but it also describes service-improvement and reasonably-necessary retention and says services are hosted in the U.S. The MCA also restricts use of Services or Output to develop a similar or competing product/service; the account owner should confirm that the intended Sentiment Desk use is within the account's permitted scope. These account-level terms must be reviewed separately from the SEC's public reuse policy.
not_cleared: Google News RSS third-party publisher titles/snippets
Yahoo Finance RSS/article content and the exact chart endpoint contract
current_followup.evidence: Read-only review of official SEC policy, SEC fair-access guidance, TypeSafe's current MCA/privacy/API documentation, and prior official-source audit notes on 2026-09-28. No credentials, databases, provider requests, or real content were accessed or transmitted.

findings.evidence: The SEC Webmaster FAQ states that EDGAR public filing content is free to access and reuse; the Website Dissemination policy says sec.gov information may be copied or further distributed without SEC permission. The SEC separately limits traffic to 10 requests per second aggregated across machines and does not allow unclassified automated tools. The app gates requests on an identifying User-Agent with contact email and paces starts at 125ms per process; no valid SEC_USER_AGENT is configured in the current environment.
findings.action: The official policy supports a narrow public-EDGAR evaluation path, subject to filing-content exceptions and non-endorsement/mark restrictions. This is not clearance for unrelated publisher feeds or proof that TypeSafe account data-use terms are acceptable.

findings.evidence: The MCA was last updated 2026-09-23. It places responsibility for input rights on the customer; credits are consumed by each submitted Input and auto-refill depends on account settings. Its telemetry definition includes hashes, summary statistics, classifications, metrics, and learnings, which may be processed without restriction to improve TypeSafe services. The privacy policy disclaims training/fine-tuning on Inputs and describes reasonably-necessary retention and U.S. hosting. The MCA also restricts use of Services or Output to develop a similar or competing product/service; application of that clause to this intended use needs account-owner or written TypeSafe clarification. The API documents 429/529 retry behavior but not a rejected-request billing exception.
findings.action: Do not enable a controlled public-source-to-Jev workflow until the authorized account owner accepts/reviews the applicable agreement and verifies account limits, auto-refill, telemetry/data-use acceptability, retention, rejected-request billing, and that the intended Sentiment Desk use is permitted under the similar/competing-product restriction. Seek written clarification from TypeSafe if needed. Historical payloads from the legacy loopback process have not been audited.

sources.name: Google News RSS
sources.identity: Feed GUID when supplied, otherwise canonical article URL, namespaced by company and collector; company matching is deterministic.
sources.time: Valid RSS pubDate is publisher-declared time; absent or invalid dates remain null. Provider retrieval and local ingestion times are stored separately.
sources.retention: Normalized title, snippet, URL, publisher, identity, time fields, adapter version, and a SHA-256 digest of parsed normalized items are stored. Raw XML is not retained; Jev replay uses normalized local observations, not raw parser input.

sources.name: Yahoo Finance RSS and chart endpoint
sources.identity: Configured symbol is the instrument key; article identity is feed GUID or canonical URL within the RSS collector.
sources.units: Price is a decimal number in the provider-returned currency; changePct is percentage change from provider previous close. No FX conversion is applied.
sources.time: Quote observation time is regularMarketTime when supplied and otherwise unknown. Local retrieval time and per-symbol last-attempt time are separate. Price-series points retain provider source timestamps and are returned only when inside the selected time window; quotes are never carried forward into synthetic time buckets.
sources.retention: Current quote snapshots and their retrieval state are in memory. Price points are stored in SQLite using source timestamps. Price-series responses disclose network, one-minute memory cache, or local-store delivery and sourceLatestAt. Raw responses are not retained.
sources.rights: High-level terms were reviewed on 2026-09-28, but the reviewed Yahoo API terms do not establish their application to these exact unofficial RSS/chart endpoints or authorize project display, retention, or model processing.

sources.name: GDELT DOC 2.0

sources.retention: Normalized item fields and a SHA-256 digest of parsed normalized items are stored; raw responses are not retained. Jev replay uses normalized local observations.
sources.rights: GDELT dataset access was reviewed at a high level. Its dataset terms do not grant rights in linked publisher content or authorize forwarding that content to TypeSafe; publisher-content permission remains unresolved.

source_rights_review.command: Verify official terms for exact Yahoo endpoints, publisher snippet retention/display/model use, SEC excerpts, and TypeSafe retention/billing configuration
source_rights_review.covers: The operator has an evidenced basis for the exact retention, display, and model-processing behavior in the live product.
source_rights_review.evidence: 2026-09-28 primary-source recheck: the SEC Webmaster FAQ says public EDGAR filing content is free to access and reuse; SEC Website Dissemination permits copying/further distribution subject to stated exceptions and no seal/endorsement implication. SEC's EDGAR access guidance requires a declared User-Agent and currently states a 10 requests/second maximum. The code validates a descriptive contact-bearing User-Agent, but none is configured, so SEC collection remains disabled. The current official TypeSafe MCA (last updated 2026-09-23) grants service-use processing during the term and perpetual processing of Telemetry, expressly including hashes, summary statistics, and classifications, and says this telemetry may be used without restriction to improve TypeSafe products; it bars use of Customer Data to train model weights without prior consent. The MCA requires the customer to hold input rights, restricts using the service/output to develop similar or competing products, and consumes credits per submitted input; opt-in auto-refill can add purchased credits. The active account owner, order/accepted terms, telemetry/retention settings, similar-product applicability, rejected-request billing, and approved spend ceiling are unverified. Yahoo's public terms reviewed do not establish permission for the exact RSS/quote/chart endpoints used by this app or the rights to retain, display, and forward their data; Google News publisher help describes publisher-feed display/link behavior but does not address this app's rights to store or forward publisher content. No non-SEC publisher permission is documented. Keep the check BLOCKED until exact source and account terms are established. Primary sources: https://www.sec.gov/about/webmaster-frequently-asked-questions ; https://www.sec.gov/about/privacy-information ; https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-search-assistance/accessing-edgar-data ; https://typesafe.ai/legal/mca ; https://legal.yahoo.com/ie/en/yahoo/terms/otos/previousversion-2025-10-18/index.html ; https://legal.yahoo.com/us/en/yahoo/terms/product-atos/apitnc/index.html ; https://support.google.com/news/publisher-center/answer/11299757?hl=en .

source_coverage.evidence: Google News RSS requests a two-day window; Finnhub default backfill is five days; Reddit requests 25 newest link posts from a one-week search and follows the provider listing after cursor one page per company/cycle; GDELT requests up to 250 English-language results from two days and records a raw response at the requested cap as partial even when invalid rows are dropped; SEC polls 8-K/8-K/A filings accepted within three days; Yahoo RSS is one provider response per ticker. X recent search follows the official next_token page chain, persists progress across scheduled cycles, and commits the newest numeric post ID only after a terminal page; its documented recent-search window is seven days. Reddit cursor behavior follows the official https://www.reddit.com/dev/api/ listing contract; the GDELT cap follows the DOC API guide at https://blog.gdeltproject.org/gdelt-doc-2-0-api-debuts/; X pagination follows the official Recent Search guide. Pagination and cap reporting do not establish exhaustive coverage, and X/Reddit/Finnhub were disabled for this checkpoint. The Desk displays “Configured feeds only. This desk does not cover the entire public web or all investor activity.” Provider rights, disabled feeds, point-in-time completeness, exact Yahoo endpoint terms, and broader exhaustive coverage remain unresolved. Latest tests establish local adapter/poller behavior only; no current provider delivery was tested. 2026-09-29 follow-up: adapter and poller regressions now preserve raw provider row counts and distinguish mixed malformed rows from wholly invalid responses for RSS, GDELT, Reddit, and Finnhub; repeated X continuation tokens fail closed; SEC missing ticker/CIK mappings are visible invalid deliveries; SEC and Yahoo chart structures are validated. Local tests do not establish live provider behavior or exhaustive source coverage.

known_gaps: Raw upstream bodies are not retained. Delivery digests cover normalized parsed items and cannot prove parser correctness or replay raw bytes; Jev replay uses normalized observation fields.

Delivery state and newest collected-item event time are separate. An old source timestamp can coexist with a current successful delivery; source age is shown, but no universal content-staleness TTL is claimed because quiet periods and provider query semantics differ.

Yahoo quote retrieval time and source regularMarketTime are separate. A failed per-symbol refresh marks the retained quote as cached and exposes its original retrieval age. Market-closure and holiday correctness is not established by the app weekday/session display.

2026-09-28 exact-source chart verification passed: only provider-timestamped points in the selected window are drawn; a real latest point outside the window is preserved as metadata and not repeated into generated display buckets.

GDELT is currently rate-limited with HTTP 429. Non-JSON bodies are rejected by the adapter and verified by tests; a post-fix live HTTP-200 non-JSON body was not observed. This is a coverage limitation, not evidence of no activity.
Optional X, Reddit, and Finnhub sources were disabled in the final live verification by explicit empty credentials. Their coverage and rights are not verified.

Official SEC policy supports reuse of public EDGAR filing content, but SEC collection is currently disabled because no descriptive SEC_USER_AGENT with contact is configured; this does not establish TypeSafe account suitability. Non-SEC publisher permission for storing/displaying snippets or sending them to Jev is not recorded; exact Yahoo endpoint rights are unclear. TypeSafe account acceptance, telemetry scope (including classifications), retention, similar/competing-product restriction, usage/refill settings, and rejected-request billing are unverified. No controlled, rights-reviewed real-source Jev evaluation is validated; saved Jev judgments exist on migrated legacy_unknown rows whose source and provider-use lineage remain unaudited.

A read-only aggregate audit of the default local database found migrated legacy_unknown observations with saved Jev judgments. Its lineage to the previously stopped 127.0.0.1:8794 process is unconfirmed. The original observation text, submitted request payloads, external request logs, credentials, and billing history were not inspected; whether publisher text was transmitted or charges incurred remains unknown.

Source collectors retry on the next scheduled poll. Jev retries only explicit retryable HTTP 429 or documented HTTP 529 rejections through persisted, bounded scheduling (maximum three attempts), honoring valid Retry-After values and otherwise exponential backoff. Transport failures, generic server errors, malformed output, and model mismatches are not automatically resubmitted. A submitted failure requires provider-usage review and explicit operator confirmation before manual retry; corrupt judgments cannot be retried. Provider coverage and pagination completeness are not proven exhaustive.

The local collector inventory is reviewed, but exhaustive public-activity coverage is not established: the source set is bounded, some collectors are optional/disabled, RSS does not expose completeness, GDELT can saturate, and direct product, hiring, app-store, search-trend, video/podcast, and support-discussion sources are not collected. Rights-cleared Jev evaluation, labeled real-source accuracy/calibration, and historical TypeSafe usage reconciliation are also incomplete.

The offline classifier evaluator consumes caller-prepared local JSON. It records the exact analyzed run digest but cannot authenticate TypeSafe receipts or independently verify reported scores/token counts; passing metrics require separate auditable provider evidence.

Provider pacing and cooldowns reduce this application's request bursts but do not verify current provider quotas, contract permissions, or behavior across multiple independent application processes. Exact provider terms and project-specific rights remain open.
